extra.message: The /vulnpy/cmdi/os-system endpoint passes attacker-controlled user_input directly to os.system(command), allowing arbitrary shell commands with the server process's privileges.
The /vulnpy/cmdi/subprocess-popen endpoint supplies user_input as command to subprocess.Popen(..., shell=True). The shell executes attacker-provided commands without validation or authentication.

When multipart middleware is enabled, POST /file-upload concatenates str(user_input[:10]) from the uploaded file into an echo command executed by os.system(). A bytes representation is not shell escaping: attacker-controlled quotes and command substitutions can execute commands despite the ten-byte truncation.

GET /thread passes the user_input query parameter to thread_function(), which concatenates it into an echo command and calls os.system(). When the Contrast imports succeed and execution reaches this sink, shell metacharacters permit arbitrary command execution in the background thread.

POST /files/upload passes the first twenty uploaded bytes to do_os_system(), which directly invokes os.system(). An unauthenticated attacker can upload a short shell command and execute it on the server.
GET /cmdi concatenates the user_input query parameter into cmd and executes it with os.system() ten times. Shell metacharacters allow unauthenticated arbitrary command execution.

POST /files/upload forwards the first twenty bytes of the uploaded file to do_os_system(), which executes them with os.system(). Truncation and catching ValueError do not prevent an attacker from supplying a valid short shell command.

The /vulnpy/unsafe_code_exec/exec endpoint passes user_input directly to exec(code). An unauthenticated request can execute arbitrary Python statements, including filesystem operations and operating-system commands.

The /vulnpy/unsafe_code_exec/eval endpoint evaluates attacker-controlled user_input with unrestricted eval(). Expressions can invoke built-ins, import modules, and execute arbitrary server-side commands.

The /vulnpy/deserialization/pickle-load endpoint encodes user_input into BytesIO and calls pickle.load(). Attacker-supplied pickle instructions can invoke arbitrary functions during deserialization; UTF-8 encoding does not prevent executable protocol-0 payloads.

The /vulnpy/deserialization/pickle-loads endpoint passes UTF-8-encoded user_input directly to pickle.loads(). An unauthenticated attacker can supply an executable pickle payload to run arbitrary code.

The /vulnpy/deserialization/yaml-load endpoint deserializes user_input with yaml.UnsafeLoader. Python object tags can invoke arbitrary callables, enabling remote code execution. Catching ConstructorError does not restrict valid executable YAML payloads.

The /vulnpy/deserialization/yaml-load-all endpoint uses yaml.UnsafeLoader on user_input and consumes the resulting generator with list(result). This constructs attacker-selected Python objects and can execute arbitrary commands during deserialization.

The /vulnpy/sqli/sqlite3-execute endpoint interpolates user_input into a quoted INSERT value before cursor.execute(sql). An attacker can terminate the value and inject additional SQL expressions or rows. The database is recreated in memory per call; persistent application-data exposure is not established.

The /vulnpy/sqli/sqlite3-executemany endpoint formats user_input directly into SQL before cursor.executemany(). Binding the separate count placeholder does not protect the interpolated value, allowing attackers to change SQL expressions and inserted rows in the per-call database.

The /vulnpy/sqli/sqlite3-executescript endpoint interpolates user_input into SQL passed to cursor.executescript(). Attackers can terminate the INSERT and execute additional SQLite statements, including ATTACH statements accessing database files permitted by the server's filesystem privileges.

The /vulnpy/pt/io-open endpoint passes user_input directly to io.open() and reads the entire file without restricting its directory. Absolute paths and traversal sequences select arbitrary readable files. HTTP handlers discard the returned contents, but attacker-selected large files or special files can exhaust memory or block the server.

The /vulnpy/pt/open endpoint passes attacker-controlled user_input to open() and performs an unlimited read. No directory restriction prevents absolute paths or traversal sequences. HTTP handlers discard the returned contents, but reading large or nonterminating special files can cause denial of service.

The /vulnpy/pt/tarfile-open endpoint uses user_input as an unrestricted filesystem path for TarFile.open(). Attackers can select archives outside the application directory and force their contents to be scanned by getmembers(). The function returns archive metadata, although HTTP handlers discard it; selecting a blocking filesystem object can stall a worker.

The /vulnpy/pt/tarfile-class endpoint supplies user_input directly to tarfile.TarFile() without a directory restriction. This permits reading and scanning attacker-selected local archives through absolute paths or traversal sequences. Returned metadata is discarded by HTTP handlers, but blocking filesystem objects can stall request processing.

The /vulnpy/pt/tarfile-bz2 endpoint opens user_input as a bzip2 archive path without restricting filesystem access. Absolute paths and traversal sequences select local archives outside the application directory, which getmembers() decompresses and scans. HTTP handlers discard returned metadata, but the filesystem access and processing remain attacker-controlled.

The legacy-urlopen, urlopen-str, and urlopen-obj routes under /vulnpy/ssrf pass attacker-controlled URLs to this urlopen sink without destination restrictions. With VULNPY_REAL_SSRF_REQUESTS enabled, as exported by the Makefile, requests can reach loopback and internal services. HTTP handlers discard the result, so this is blind SSRF.

The /vulnpy/ssrf/httpconnection-init and httpsconnection-init endpoints pass user_input as the connection host and issue a GET request without validating the destination. Real connections are enabled by the Makefile's VULNPY_REAL_SSRF_REQUESTS setting, allowing blind requests to attacker-selected internal hosts and ports.

The /vulnpy/redos/re-fullmatch endpoint applies the nested-quantifier pattern ((a)+)+ to user_input using re.fullmatch(). A long run of 'a' characters followed by a nonmatching character causes exponential backtracking. No input limit or execution timeout prevents CPU exhaustion.

The /vulnpy/redos/re-fullmatch-compiled endpoint performs a full match of ((a)+)+ against attacker-controlled user_input. A long sequence of 'a' characters ending in a nonmatching character triggers exponential backtracking; compiling the pattern does not prevent request-driven CPU exhaustion.

At /vulnpy/xss/raw, the user_input query parameter is concatenated into HTML without escaping and returned with content_type='text/html'. A crafted link executes attacker-provided script in the application's origin.

The /vulnpy/xss/raw handler concatenates user_input from GET parameters or POST form data into the returned HTML without escaping. Attacker-supplied tags and event handlers execute in the application's origin.

The /vulnpy/xss/raw handler appends user_input from request.GET or request.POST directly to HTML passed to HttpResponse(). Django template autoescaping is bypassed, allowing reflected script execution.

The asynchronous /vulnpy/xss/raw handler concatenates attacker-controlled user_input into HTML returned through HttpResponse(). No escaping occurs, so a crafted request can execute script in a victim's browser.

The /vulnpy/xss and /vulnpy/xss/raw handlers pass req.get_param('user_input') to _set_xss_response(), which concatenates it into resp.text and sets text/html. Unescaped attacker-provided markup enables reflected XSS.

The asynchronous /vulnpy/xss and /vulnpy/xss/raw handlers forward the user_input query parameter to this unescaped HTML concatenation. Returning the result as text/html permits attacker-controlled script execution in the application's origin.

The /vulnpy/xss/raw route interpolates the user_input query parameter into markup returned through HTMLResponse(). The str annotation does not escape HTML, allowing reflected XSS through a crafted URL.
The /vulnpy/xss/raw handler inserts user_input from query parameters, form data, or the User-Input header into HTML without escaping. Flask returns this string as HTML, enabling reflected XSS.

The /vulnpy/xss/raw handler concatenates user_input from request.GET or request.POST into HTML returned by Response(). No output encoding prevents attacker-controlled markup from executing in a browser.

The /vulnpy/xss/raw handler appends user_input from query parameters or the User_Input header to its HTML response without escaping. A crafted URL can execute attacker-controlled script in the application's origin.

At /vulnpy/xss/raw, user_input parsed from QUERY_STRING is formatted into a paragraph and returned with Content-Type: text/html. Because the value is not HTML-escaped, attacker-supplied tags or event handlers execute in the victim's browser.

GET /template-xss/jinja renders request.args['user_input'] into an HTML response using a Jinja environment without autoescaping. apps/templates/jinja/xss.html:30 also marks user_input as safe, so attacker-supplied markup executes as reflected XSS.

The unauthenticated /async_will_block asynchronous handler calls time.sleep(10), blocking its worker's event loop for ten seconds per request. Repeated requests prevent that worker from processing other asynchronous requests.

POST /files/upload reads the complete attacker-supplied UploadFile into a bytes object with await file.read(), without enforcing a file-size limit. A sufficiently large upload can exhaust server memory even though only twenty bytes are subsequently used.

cwe: CWE-789: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value

extra.message: Every unauthenticated GET /thread starts a new operating-system thread without a pool or concurrency limit. Each thread sleeps for at least two seconds, including when Contrast is unavailable, allowing rapid requests to accumulate threads and exhaust process resources.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: The runnable Django application enables DEBUG=True, including when loaded through WSGI. Invalid input to uncaught trigger operations can generate detailed error pages exposing source excerpts, filesystem paths, local variables, and configuration information.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Successful responses explicitly send Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=0. When served over HTTPS, this removes a browser's dynamically stored HSTS policy for the host, weakening protection against subsequent HTTP downgrade attacks.
